question: The refractive indices of turpentine oil and glass are 1.47 and 1.52, respectively. A ray of light passes from turpentine oil to glass. The refractive index of glass with respect to turpentine oil is _______ and the ray bends _______ the normal in glass.
solution: The correct answer is __**1.03, towards**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The **refractive index** of a medium is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced when it travels through that medium compared to a vacuum. • The refractive index of turpentine oil is given as **1.47**, and the refractive index of glass is given as **1.52**. • The **refractive index of glass with respect to turpentine oil** is calculated using the formula: **Refractive index (glass w.r.t. turpentine oil) = (Refractive index of glass) / (Refractive index of turpentine oil)** = 1.52 / 1.47 ≈ **1.03**. • **When light travels from a medium with a lower refractive index (turpentine oil) to a medium with a higher refractive index (glass)**, it bends **towards the normal**. This is because the speed of light decreases as it enters the denser medium (glass). • *Hence, the correct refractive index is 1.03, and the light bends towards the normal.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __ • **Refractive Index:** • The refractive index is a dimensionless quantity and is a fundamental property of transparent materials. • It is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the given medium. Formula:** n = c/v**, where **c** is the speed of light in a vacuum, and **v** is the speed of light in the medium. • **Snell's Law:** • Snell's Law governs the refraction of light as it passes between two media with different refractive indices. It states: **n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂**, where **n₁** and **n₂** are the refractive indices of the two media, and θ₁ and θ₂ are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively. • If n₂ > n₁, the light bends **towards the normal**. If n₂ • **Practical Applications of Refractive Index:** • Used in designing lenses for spectacles, cameras, and microscopes to control the bending of light. • Helps in determining the purity of liquids like oils and alcohols based on their refractive indices. • Plays a crucial role in fiber optics technology for efficient signal transmission. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** • **Refractive Index of Common Materials:** • **Vacuum:** 1 (absolute reference). • **Air:** Approximately 1.0003 (close to vacuum). • **Water:** 1.33. • **Glass:** Varies between 1.5 to 1.9 depending on the type of glass. • **Bending of Light:** • Light bends towards the normal when it enters a denser medium (higher refractive index). • Light bends away from the normal when it enters a rarer medium (lower refractive index). • **Critical Angle and Total Internal Reflection:** • The critical angle is the angle of incidence beyond which light is totally reflected back into the denser medium. • This phenomenon is used in **optical fibers** and **prism-based instruments**. 277:T2476,
